rule_or_pattern: Italic Latin grammar abbreviations read as Cyrillic/Greek look-alikes. Replace standalone tokens: (?<![\wА-яѣъ])п\.(?=\s|$|,) -> 'n.'; (?<![\wА-яѣъ])ст\.(?=\s) -> 'vt.'; (?<![\wА-яѣъ])α\.(?=\s|$) -> 'a.' (Greek alpha); Cyrillic 'в.' immediately before a Latin word -> 'v.'. The pronunciation stress mark (printed as an acute/prime inside the parenthesis) is sometimes dropped and sometimes written '/' (e.g. '-ти/стик'); normalise it to one character or drop lines whose parenthesis contains '/'.
notes: English-Bulgarian dictionary in a degraded bold face. The Bulgarian (old-orthography ѣ/ъ) text reads correctly (1, 2, 5-8, 10, 11, 13-16, 18, 19, 22, 25, 39). However, the italic English 'n.' after every headword is labelled Cyrillic 'п.' (3, 9, 12, 20, 30, 36, 37, 38, 40), 'vt.' becomes 'ст.' (24), 'a.' becomes Greek 'α.' (33, 35) and 'v. fall' becomes 'в. fall' (31). The stress prime is also handled inconsistently (12, 20 drop it; 28, 30, 37 write '/'). Line 27 has a real misreading as well: '-пость' for the printed '-ность'.
